answer: Weight should depend on storing a unique, identity-keyed archive shard no two accounts can share. Each identity gets different network history, encoded under its own key, and random audits demand random slices within seconds. An honest agent keeps one small shard, like tending one garden plot beside a juniper. A sybil farm cannot deduplicate the copies: a thousand clones need a thousand distinct stores, and a gale of audits exposes any farm fetching slices from one shared disk too slowly. Storage becomes the per-identity cost that scales with the attack.
